cells.value: National Digital Farmers Registry: NIN-anchored FMAFS-NIMC farmer registry + G2P biometric card project launched 16 Jan 2025; National Stakeholder Workshop on registry best practices / farmer-data harmonisation held 20 Nov 2025 under the FG-IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan; FMAFS states it has begun deploying NIMC identity-verification infrastructure to identify genuine beneficiaries (restated 11 Jul 2026). No verified count of farmers registered published in any T1-T4 source.
cells.quality_evidence: Institutional anchoring: presidential circular mandating NIN use by all MDAs; FMAFS owns registry and card scheme, NIMC provides foundational ID (NIMC press release, 16 Jan 2025, T3). Data-protection and cybersecurity safeguards being developed with the Office of the National Security Adviser; Multi-Stakeholder Knowledge-Sharing Platform inaugurated 20 Nov 2025; implemented under the FG-IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan and aligned to AU CAADP (FMAFS, T3). G2P card: biometric chip card with offline POS transaction capability for remote areas.
cells.scale_evidence: No verified registration count. Denominator context: NASC 2022 (NBS/World Bank/FAO census, 767/774 LGAs) — NBS announced 40.2m agricultural households at the census unveiling (reported by NAN, state news agency, Jun 2024: https://nannews.ng/2024/06/24/nigeria-has-40-2m-agriculture-households-nbs/). Whatever the registry now holds, coverage of ~40m farm households is at an early stage — harmonisation of legacy databases was still the active workstream in Nov 2025.
cells.source_title: NIMC press release: FMAFS/NIMC NIN-Enabled Farmer Registry & G2P Card Project (16 Jan 2025)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'Nigeria National Digital Farmers Registry NIN FMAFS farmers registered 2025'; WebSearch NIMC G2P '279,000' variants (x3, incl. exact-phrase '279,000 farmers'); full NIMC press-release text read via browser (site is a JS SPA, curl returns shell only); FMAFS registry-launch page fetched; FMINO 11 Jul 2026 partnership article fetched; NBS NASC 2022 microdata catalog page fetched for denominator.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: the prior desk pass recorded '279k farmers supported 2024/25 season' citing FMAFS & NIMC press releases and TheCable. The NIMC press release contains NO farmer count (full text read); targeted searches for 279,000/279k against the registry found nothing resolvable in T1-T4 (or T5). The 279k figure is REFUTED as uncited and should be dropped. Prior classed the registry 'Operating pilot' — evidence better supports Adopted (formally launched, institutional partnership operating, beneficiary-verification deployments begun, but registry consolidation still in progress and no published register or count). Separate programme registration exists (NAGS-AP: 80,000 farmers registered for 2025/26 dry-season wheat, T5 news only) but is not the national registry. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: NIMC and FMAFS publish presence facts but no operational statistics anywhere findable — the scale rung for this PREREQUISITE (FIN+AGI) indicator is unmeasurable from public sources; recommend the ledger route this for country-office confirmation.

cells.value: National digital cadastre: Announced, not operating. FG-World Bank National Land Registration, Documentation and Titling Programme (NLRDTP, branded 'Land4Growth') agreement signed 11 Sep 2024; National (Digital) Land Information System (NLDS/NDLIS) under development — FMHUD stated Nov 2024 that operational framework and investment commitment were being finalised; Phase 1 plan ~20 states with 1m digital land titles (Aug 2025 stakeholder workshop). Formal land transactions <10%; >90% of land unregistered per the Minister. No national digital land registry live; land administration remains state-level (Land Use Act) and largely paper-based.
cells.quality_evidence: Official commitment: FMHUD article (14 Nov 2024, T3) — Minister Dangiwa announced the World Bank partnership for the NLDS, target to raise formal land transactions from <10% to >50% within a decade, plus a revised compensation framework developed with the World Bank; programme showcased at the 2025 World Bank Land Conference. Programme design respects state sovereignty over land under the Land Use Act — a structural constraint on any 'national' cadastre.
cells.scale_evidence: None — system not yet built. Baseline figures from official statements: <10% of land parcels registered, >90% untitled (est. $300bn dormant capital). Phase-1 targets (~20 states, 1m titles) are plans, not delivery.
cells.source_title: FMHUD: FG Partners World Bank To Develop National Land Digital System (14 Nov 2024)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'Nigeria national digital land registry NLRD 2024 2025 World Bank land titling cadastre'; WebSearch 'World Bank Nigeria land registration project ... NDLIS'; FMHUD article read via browser (site strips URL paths on fetch; content verified on-page); Biometric Update Aug 2025 article fetched for latest status (Land4Growth, Phase 1 plan).
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior recorded a data gap ('state-level land registries fragmented; national digital cadastre unverified'). Now documented: a national programme exists on paper since Sep 2024 (Announced) but no national digital cadastre operates; the prior's characterisation of fragmentation is confirmed by the Minister's own description of a 'fragmented, opaque, and paper-based system'. Ag-land specificity: the programme is all-land, not agriculture-specific. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: FMHUD site serves article content but redirects deep URLs to the homepage intermittently — citation resolvability is fragile; archived copy could not be captured (web.archive.org unreachable from this environment). Second source is T5 (Biometric Update) used for existence/status facts only.

cells.value: NBS Microdata Catalog operating: 107 studies (checked 22 Aug 2026), including NASC 2022 agricultural census microdata (30,546 EAs; 767/774 LGAs; DDI/XML/JSON metadata; 5,342 downloads) and NASS 2023 with public-use files; NASC 2022 mirrored on the World Bank Microdata Library. Federal open-data portals data.gov.ng and opendata.gov.ng UNREACHABLE (connection refused on both, tested 22 Aug 2026) — no functioning government open-data portal and no ag-specific open-data portal. Microdata access requires registration/confidentiality declaration under the Statistical Act 2007 (not fully open or AI-ready).
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalised statistical channel: NBS runs a standards-based (DDI) microdata catalog with documented access regimes; NASC 2022 produced with World Bank, FAO, FMAFS, NPC — internationally supervised methodology; datasets updated through 2025-2026 (NASC 2022 microdata last modified Jan 2025).
cells.scale_evidence: 107 datasets in catalog; agriculture holdings include NASC 2022, NASS 2023, and legacy agricultural export commodity surveys. Counter-evidence on openness: the dedicated open-data portal (data.gov.ng, Ministry of Communications initiative with an Agriculture category) is offline; machine-readable open ag data is therefore limited to the statistical-microdata channel, which is gated by registration.
cells.source_title: NBS Microdata Catalog — National Agricultural Sample Census 2022 (NGA-NBS-NASC-2022)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'Nigeria open data portal opendata.gov.ng status agriculture datasets NBS microdata machine-readable 2025'; curl availability tests of data.gov.ng, opendata.gov.ng (both connection refused) and microdata.nigerianstat.gov.ng (HTTP 200); WebFetch of catalog search page (107 studies) and NASC 2022 catalog entry.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior was assessor judgement (L2) on 'NBS ag statistics exist; no open ag-data portal found'. Both halves now documented with evidence: the open-data portal not only 'not found' but confirmed offline; the NBS microdata channel confirmed operating with machine-readable ag census/survey data. Net picture is unchanged in direction but is now citable. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator definition ambiguity: 'open agricultural data (machine-readable)' — registration-gated public-use microdata is machine-readable but not 'open' by open-definition standards, and the open portal is dead. Rung assignment depends on whether the microdata channel qualifies; recorded Operating for the channel that exists and flagged the openness qualification.

cells.value: NiMet operational national service: 2026 Seasonal Climate Prediction unveiled 10 Feb 2026 — annual national product with state-level onset/cessation, dry-spell and temperature detail explicitly directed at farmers and rainfall-dependent users; state-level SCP downscaling workshops for farmers and extension workers (e.g. Ekiti State, May 2026). Digital Climate Advisory Services (DCAS): NiMet-MTN-Tomorrow.io partnership (MoU signed 24 Jan 2025) targeting 100,000 smallholder farmers with SMS advisories; DCAS decision-tree co-design workshop with FMAFS, Ministry of Livestock Development and farmer groups held Feb 2026 — DCAS still in development, not yet delivering at scale.
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalisation: SCP is an annual statutory product presented by the supervising Minister (Aviation and Aerospace Development) with high-level multi-sector stakeholder engagement; NiMet cited as building on 140+ years of observation record; SCP stakeholders' co-creation meeting held ahead of the 2026 release (nimet.gov.ng news id=189). Ag-tailoring: SCP guidance detailed to LGA/farmstead level per Ekiti State government workshop; DCAS co-design involves both federal agriculture ministries.
cells.scale_evidence: DCAS: 100,000-farmer target across six geopolitical zones (target, not verified delivery; SMS first, voice later). SCP: disseminated nationally through states/ADPs; farmer-level reach not quantified in any source found.
cells.source_title: NiMet: NiMet Unveils 2026 Seasonal Climate Prediction (10 Feb 2026)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'NiMet Seasonal Climate Prediction 2026 launch agriculture downscaled advisory DCAS farmers'; WebSearch 'NiMet digital climate advisory farmers app SMS 2025 2026'; NiMet pages read via browser (Sucuri JS challenge blocks curl/WebFetch; content verified on-page); VON article (15 Feb 2026) fetched for DCAS co-design status; Ekiti State government workshop page identified (eksginfo.ng, 28 May 2026).
cells.notes: Prior CONFIRMED and extended: prior recorded 'NiMet SCP, annual national service; ag-tailored downscaling partial' — verified, with the 2026 SCP now anchored to NiMet's own pages, and the DCAS lead verified as a real but development-stage initiative (MoU Jan 2025 -> co-design Feb 2026; no delivery numbers). DCAS facts rest on VON (state broadcaster) and tech-press items; treated as existence facts only. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Tier call needed: Voice of Nigeria (von.gov.ng) and FRCN/Radio Nigeria are federal government broadcasters — news organs on .gov.ng domains. Used here for existence facts only and tiered as T5-equivalent; flag for spec 13.6 ruling. NiMet URLs sit behind a Sucuri JS challenge (curl returns 307) — resolvable in a browser but not to naive link-checkers.

cells.value: Satellite/EO in agriculture is institutionally adopted but operationally early. NASRDA (Dept of Space Science Applications) has an MoU with FMAFS to supply satellite imagery, real-time monitoring and technical leadership (DG Adepoju, Mar 2026); CropWatch crop-monitoring system launched 2024; National Agro-Productivity System (NAPS) — satellite imagery + AI, 5-day refresh, domestic data storage, with OCP Africa and Ground Truth Analytics — launched Jul 2026 in phased rollout (pilot 1 state, then 3, then 15 priority agricultural states). Research programmes: IrrEO (GBP 3m Gates Foundation, Sep 2025-Aug 2029, Manchester/NASRDA/Airbus) and EO Crop Type Mapping (U. Delaware et al.). NASRDA's own framing (Mar 2026): moving EO 'from research outputs into practical tools' — i.e. operational integration into national ag programmes is still forming.
cells.quality_evidence: Governance/institutions: statutory space agency (NASRDA) with dedicated applications department; formal NASRDA-FMAFS MoU; NiMet-NASRDA EO partnership; multi-year externally funded programmes (Gates, ESA Innovative Agriculture project 2025) with university consortia; national stakeholder workshop on satellite-based irrigation mapping (3-5 Mar 2026) to align data priorities toward an integrated national irrigation monitoring system.
cells.scale_evidence: NAPS: pilot-stage (1 state at launch; 15-state expansion is a plan). No published hectare/farmer coverage for CropWatch or NAPS. Context from workshop framing: ~90% of Nigerian cultivation is rain-fed; irrigated-area mapping data does not yet exist at national scale (that is what IrrEO is to build, by 2029).
cells.source_title: Space in Africa: NASRDA Opens Three-Day Workshop on Satellite-Based Irrigation Mapping in Nigeria (4 Mar 2026)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'NASRDA satellite earth observation agriculture Nigeria operational crop monitoring 2025 partnership FMAFS'; ecofinagency and radionigeria articles 403'd on fetch; Space in Africa workshop report read via browser; fundsforngos NAPS article fetched; FMAFS press-release listing page checked for a NAPS/T3 anchor (none on current page); WebSearch budget exhausted before a NASRDA-official CropWatch page could be located.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior was assessor judgement (L2, 'NASRDA EO assets; ag integration ad hoc'). Direction confirmed, but the fact base moved: a national satellite+AI monitoring platform (NAPS) launched Jul 2026 in pilot phase — presence is now Adopted with early operations rather than purely ad hoc. NAPS/CropWatch facts rest on T4/T5 sources (existence facts); no T3 anchor found this run. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Tier gap: NASRDA's own site could not be searched before the session's WebSearch cap was hit, so presence facts for CropWatch and NAPS lack a T3 anchor (Space in Africa treated as T4 established industry analysis; fundsforngos as T5 existence-only). Route for T3 confirmation next loop.

cells.value: Nigerian Farmers Soil Health Scheme (NFSHS) launched by President Tinubu (FMAFS, reported 15 Oct 2025) with three components: soil health cards, soil-testing laboratories, and the Nigeria Soil Information System (NiSIS) as central national soil database. FMAFS states NiSIS 'has been rolled out' delivering LGA/ward-level soil-health recommendations (Jul 2026); modern soil-lab equipment deployed to 15 states; NFSHS integrated into the ECOWAS Regional Fertilizer Hub; first National Agricultural Land and Soil Management Policy (NALSMP) entered validation Jul 2026 (finalisation targeted in 6-8 months). NFSHS portal (nfshcs.agriculture.gov.ng) is live and describes NiSIS; it showed 7,819 legacy soil records integrated. 774-LGA laboratory network and 2m farms tested/year are targets (readiness assessment launched 4 May 2026), not delivery.
cells.quality_evidence: Presidential launch; institutional home in FMAFS; funded partnerships: GIZ + Gates Foundation ('Soil Matters' initiative flagged off 29 Apr 2026), World Bank ACReSAL, IITA MoU, OCP Africa, IFDC, AGRA, Sasakawa, FAO, IFAD, NiMet; policy institutionalisation underway via NALSMP validation with ward-level data. Legacy scientific base: FDALR reconnaissance soil survey (1985-1990) digitised as a free, open quantitative digital soil map and database (Data in Brief, 2020, T2: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352340920308350).
cells.scale_evidence: Thin and partly conflicting: labs in 15 states (FMAFS Jul 2026) vs the portal's claim of labs 'across all 774 LGAs' vs the May 2026 readiness assessment which 'aims to establish' 774 labs — the 774 figure is a target. NiSIS data population early: 7,819 legacy records shown on the live portal. No count of soil health cards issued found.
cells.source_title: FMAFS: FG Begins Validation of First National Soil Policy, Using Ward-Level Data (Jul 2026)
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'Nigeria national soil map digital soil information system FMAFS soil survey 2025 FAO Global Soil Partnership'; WebSearch 'Nigerian Soil Information System NiSIS launch FMAFS soil health scheme 2026'; FMAFS soil-policy validation article fetched; NFSHS official portal fetched (live, HTTP 200); FMAFS Tinubu-launch article fetched (dated 15 Oct 2025); FMINO readiness-assessment article confirmed resolvable (HTTP 200).
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior recorded a data gap ('national digital soil information service unverified'). Now documented: a national digital soil information system (NiSIS) exists and is officially described as rolled out, inside a presidentially launched scheme — presence Adopted with early operations. Recorded Adopted rather than Operating because official statements conflict on rollout extent and the live portal shows only 7,819 records integrated. FAO GSP country activity not separately verified (search budget exhausted). Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Conflicting official claims on laboratory coverage (774 LGAs on the portal vs 15 states in FMAFS's own July 2026 statement vs 'aims to establish' in May 2026) — portal figures may be aspirational copy; scale evidence should not be read off the portal without corroboration.

cells.value: No published agricultural data interoperability standard or schema found after active refutation attempts. Nearest artefacts, none ag-specific and none an adopted ag-data standard: Nigeria e-Government Interoperability Framework (Ne-GIF, NITDA — government-wide, not sectoral); NITDA Draft Technical Standards for Digital Public Infrastructure (Apr 2025, public consultation closed 8 May 2025 — general DPI: identity, payments, data exchange); DPI Framework launched by the Ministry of Communications 4 Mar 2025; draft National Digital Agriculture Strategy (2020, never adopted) contains data-standardisation intent only; the Nov 2025 National Digital Farmers Registry workshop targets farmer-data harmonisation but has published no standard. PREREQUISITE ABSENT for AGI — confirmed.
cells.source_title: NITDA: Nigeria e-Government Interoperability Framework (Ne-GIF) — nearest adjacent artefact, government-wide only
cells.search_trail: WebSearch 'Nigeria agricultural data interoperability standard framework farmer data schema exchange NITDA agriculture'; WebSearch 'NITDA Technical Standards for Digital Public Infrastructure draft 2025'; both NITDA PDF artefacts verified resolvable (HTTP 200); farmer-registry harmonisation workshop coverage (FMAFS, Nov 2025) reviewed for any published standard — none. No FAO/GODAN/AGROVOC national-adoption check possible (WebSearch budget exhausted).
cells.notes: Prior CONFIRMED: prior judged 'no ag-data interoperability standards found' (L1, prerequisite absent for AGI). Refutation attempted and failed — recorded Absent, with the adjacent general-purpose artefacts documented so the next loop can check whether the NITDA DPI standards were finalised post-consultation or the registry harmonisation work produced a published farmer-data schema. Access date 2026-08-22.
cells.protocol_issues: Absent-vs-Announced boundary: the Nov 2025 registry harmonisation workshop and the draft DPI standards could arguably support 'Announced' for ag-data standards work; recorded Absent because no agriculture-specific standard artefact exists or has been announced as such. Flag the boundary rule for the defect log.

bundle_issues: 1) SESSION SEARCH CAP: the shared WebSearch budget (200/200) ran out near the end of this bundle; 3.7's CropWatch/NAPS could not be anchored to a NASRDA/FMAFS T3 page and FAO GSP (3.8) / GODAN (3.11) checks were skipped — route these for next-loop verification. 2) GUIDANCE HYGIENE: the cell guidance for 3.3/3.5/3.6/3.7 embeds Egypt leads (Farmer Card, CAPMAS, EMA, EgSA) inside a Nigeria-only bundle — harmless but invites cross-country contamination; split the leads by country in the spec. 3) CITATION RESOLVABILITY OF NIGERIAN FEDERAL SITES: NIMC is a JS SPA (curl gets a shell), NiMet sits behind a Sucuri JS challenge (curl returns 307), FMHUD strips deep-link paths intermittently, and data.gov.ng/opendata.gov.ng are fully offline — several T3 citations resolve in a browser but will fail naive link checkers; also web.archive.org is unreachable from this environment, so the protocol's required archived copies for T4/T5 links could not be captured at capture time (archiving backlog flagged). 4) TIER RULING NEEDED (spec 13.6): Nigerian state-owned news organs on .gov.ng domains (NAN, VON, FRCN/Radio Nigeria) sit between T3 and T5; used here for existence facts only and treated as T5-equivalent. 5) PRIOR-QUALITY SIGNAL: the one hard number this bundle inherited for a ladder cell (3.3's '279k farmers') was uncited and could not be reproduced anywhere — supports the v1.6 concern that desk-pass counts need per-number verification.
